note: GER: troops enter the demilitarized zone 7 Mar 1936 under Blomberg's directive of 2 Mar; Locarno denounced the same day. WEST: Cabinet approval of the Defence Requirements Committee programme (Feb 1936) and the Statement Relating to Defence of 3 Mar 1936. The French and British decisions of 7 to 19 Mar 1936 not to act are the realized non-resistance; the catalogue offers resist_rhineland only at tick 1 [SQR]. USSR: idle (the French Chamber ratified the Franco-Soviet pact on 27 Feb 1936, a French act). JPN: idle (the army mutiny of 26 Feb 1936 is domestic).
source: DGFP Series C vol. V (German memorandum to the Locarno powers, 7 Mar 1936); Cmd. 5107 (3 Mar 1936); DDF 2e serie vol. I; CAB 23 conclusions of Feb and Mar 1936

note: WEST: resist_rhineland is available at this tick and is not taken; this row is where the model records the non-resistance decided 7 to 19 Mar 1936 (Sarraut government 7 to 8 Mar; London meeting of the Locarno powers and League Council finding of a breach, 19 Mar). GER: the peace proposals of 31 Mar and the unanswered British questionnaire of 6 May 1936 have no catalogue action. Nature: locarno_lapses is not yet available (it waits until the resistance window has passed).
source: DDF 2e serie vol. I; League of Nations Official Journal, Council minutes of Mar 1936; HC Deb 9 Mar 1936 (Eden's statement)

note: GER: Hitler's memorandum on the Four-Year Plan (Aug 1936: armed forces operational within four years) and the army's armament programme of Aug 1936; two-year service decreed 24 Aug 1936. With delay 8 the effect (arms_GER high) is visible at tick 11. WEST: the French four-year programme of 7 Sep 1936 falls under the WEST rearm already pending from tick 0. Nature: locarno_lapses [SQR, historical date 19 Mar 1936]: the earliest tick at which the catalogue lets the treaty regime lapse after an unresisted remilitarization. The Spanish Civil War (from 17 Jul 1936) is not modeled.
source: Four-Year Plan memorandum, Aug 1936 (text in Treue, Vierteljahrshefte fuer Zeitgeschichte 1955); Tooze 2006; Deist in Germany and the Second World War vol. I

note: GER: October Protocols signed by Ciano and Neurath 23 Oct 1936; Mussolini's Milan speech naming the Axis 1 Nov 1936. JPN: Anti-Comintern Pact signed in Berlin 25 Nov 1936; Germany is the counterparty, and the catalogue gives the act to JPN so that GER's one action this quarter is the Axis. WEST: rearm pending. Belgium's return to neutrality (14 Oct 1936) is not modeled.
source: DGFP Series C vol. V and VI; Ciano's diplomatic papers; Anti-Comintern Pact text of 25 Nov 1936

note: Anglo-Italian Gentlemen's Agreement 2 Jan 1937 (italy_reconciles is no longer available once axis holds). The Defence Loans Act (Feb to Mar 1937) belongs to the WEST rearm already pending. Kandelaki's approaches to Schacht for Stalin (Dec 1936 to early 1937) were turned down by Hitler; they are the earliest record of the German-Soviet alternative and are idle here.
source: Hansard 1937 (Defence Loans Bill); DGFP Series C vol. VI

note: Nature: Tukhachevsky and seven senior commanders arrested in May, tried and shot 11 to 12 Jun 1937; the purge of the officer corps ran through 1938. WEST: arms_WEST rising is visible from this tick (decision of tick 0). Chamberlain became Prime Minister 28 May 1937.
source: Soviet press announcements of 11 to 12 Jun 1937; Erickson 1962

note: JPN: war with China from 7 Jul 1937 (Marco Polo Bridge), not modeled in v0. Blomberg's directive of 24 Jun 1937 (1937Q2) already listed a Czech contingency (Case Green) as a planning case.
source: Nuremberg document C-175 (directive of 24 Jun 1937)

note: GER: the conference of 5 Nov 1937 recorded by Hossbach is a statement of aims (and the occasion of a steel-allocation dispute), not a catalogue action; GER rearm is pending until tick 10. WEST: Halifax's visit to Hitler 19 Nov 1937 (the general-settlement approach) has no catalogue action. Italy joined the Anti-Comintern Pact 6 Nov 1937.
source: Nuremberg document 386-PS (Hossbach memorandum, 10 Nov 1937); DBFP Second Series

note: GER: Berchtesgaden meeting with Schuschnigg 12 Feb 1938; plebiscite announced 9 Mar; Case Otto directive 11 Mar; troops entered 12 Mar; reunification law 13 Mar 1938. Mussolini's acquiescence was conveyed on 11 Mar. USSR: Litvinov's public proposal of 17 Mar 1938 for collective action has no USSR catalogue action; the British refusal (Chamberlain in the Commons, 24 Mar 1938) is WEST idle.
source: Nuremberg document C-102 (Case Otto, 11 Mar 1938); DGFP Series D vol. I; HC Deb 24 Mar 1938

note: GER: decision record is the Case Green directive of 30 May 1938 ('my unalterable decision to smash Czechoslovakia by military action in the near future'), after Hitler's instructions to Henlein of 28 Mar and the Karlsbad programme of 24 Apr 1938; the May crisis of 20 to 22 May. The cession demand itself was put in September (tick 10). WEST: the British warning to Berlin of 21 May is idle.
source: Nuremberg document 388-PS (Case Green, 30 May 1938); DGFP Series D vol. II; DBFP Third Series vol. I

note: GER: Nuremberg speech 12 Sep, Berchtesgaden 15 Sep, Godesberg memorandum 23 Sep 1938 (the cession demand). WEST: Anglo-French proposals to Prague 19 Sep; Munich agreement signed in the early hours of 30 Sep 1938. concede reads last_GER == demand_sudeten, which the tick 9 decision satisfies. GER's documented alternative this quarter was Case Green (attack_czechoslovakia, readiness by 1 Oct 1938), held until 28 Sep. USSR: Soviet statements of readiness to aid Czechoslovakia (Litvinov at the League Assembly, 21 Sep 1938) have no catalogue action.
source: DGFP Series D vol. II; DBFP Third Series vol. II; CAB 23 conclusions of 17 to 30 Sep 1938; Munich agreement of 29 Sep 1938

note: GER: Goering's conference of 14 Oct 1938 announcing Hitler's order for a greatly enlarged armaments programme (the Z-Plan followed in Jan 1939); with delay 8 its effect falls at tick 20, the horizon. Second GER actions of the quarter: the directive of 21 Oct 1938 on the remainder of Czechoslovakia (behind tick 12) and the Danzig proposal put to Lipski on 24 Oct 1938. arms_GER high is visible from this tick (decision of tick 2). WEST: British post-Munich acceleration (air expansion scheme approved Nov 1938) and the French decree-laws of Nov 1938; arms_WEST high visible at tick 16.
source: Nuremberg document 1301-PS (14 Oct 1938); Nuremberg document C-136 (21 Oct 1938); CAB 23 conclusions of Oct and Nov 1938

note: GER: Slovak declaration of independence 14 Mar; Hacha in Berlin 14 to 15 Mar; troops entered Prague 15 Mar 1939. Memel (22 to 23 Mar) is a second GER action, not modeled. WEST: British proposal of 20 Mar 1939 for a four-power declaration (Britain, France, the USSR, Poland), after Litvinov's proposal of 18 Mar for a conference; Poland declined to sign with the USSR. The Polish guarantee was also decided this quarter (31 Mar); it reacts to Prague through belief_WEST and is placed at tick 13 [SQR].
source: DGFP Series D vol. IV and VI; DBFP Third Series vol. IV; Chamberlain's Birmingham speech, 17 Mar 1939

note: WEST: guarantee_poland [SQR, historical date 31 Mar 1939, Cabinet of 30 Mar and the Prime Minister's Commons statement of 31 Mar]; the belief flip caused by Prague is visible only at this tick. The WEST decisions that belong to 1939Q2 (conscription announced 26 Apr; the Cabinet decision of 24 May to negotiate an alliance with the USSR) cannot also be placed: one action per tick. GER: Weizsaecker's instruction to Schulenburg of 30 May 1939 to open political talks with Moscow; also this quarter: Case White directive of 3 Apr, renunciation of the German-Polish declaration 28 Apr, Pact of Steel 22 May, conference of 23 May. USSR: Litvinov replaced by Molotov 3 May; the Soviet triple-alliance proposal of 17 Apr is not an acceptance of the WEST approach and is recorded as idle. JPN: the Nomonhan fighting from 11 May 1939 was a Kwantung Army escalation, not a strike_north decision.
source: CAB 23 conclusions of 30 Mar 1939; HC Deb 31 Mar 1939; DGFP Series D vol. VI; Nuremberg documents C-120 (3 Apr 1939) and L-79 (23 May 1939)

note: USSR: agreement to Ribbentrop's visit 19 to 21 Aug; non-aggression pact and secret protocol signed 23 Aug 1939; German-Soviet credit agreement 19 Aug. GER: Directive No. 1 of 31 Aug; invasion 1 Sep 1939 (an attack ordered for 26 Aug was halted on 25 Aug). WEST: British and French declarations of war 3 Sep 1939; available here because the guarantee is in force. The Soviet invasion of eastern Poland (17 Sep) is a second USSR action of the quarter, placed at tick 15. The Anglo-French military mission in Moscow (11 to 21 Aug) has no row; in this replay accept_alliance is not available to the USSR here because last_WEST is the guarantee. JPN: Nomonhan ceasefire 15 Sep 1939.
source: DGFP Series D vol. VII; Nazi-Soviet Relations 1939-1941 (Department of State, 1948); Trevor-Roper (ed.), Hitler's War Directives, Directive No. 1; CAB 23 conclusions of 1 to 3 Sep 1939

note: GER: Directive No. 6 of 9 Oct 1939 ordering preparation of an offensive through Luxembourg, Belgium and the Netherlands. Hitler's Reichstag offer of 6 Oct 1939 (offer_terms_britain), rejected by Chamberlain 12 Oct, is a second GER action. USSR: occupy_east_poland [SQR, historical date 17 Sep 1939]; boundary and friendship treaty 28 Sep. Nature: Neutrality Act of 4 Nov 1939 (cash and carry for arms). The Winter War (from 30 Nov 1939) is not modeled. WEST: rearm pending.
source: Trevor-Roper (ed.), Hitler's War Directives, Directive No. 6; HC Deb 12 Oct 1939; Neutrality Act of 4 Nov 1939

note: GER: the offensive was postponed repeatedly from Nov 1939 (weather; the Mechelen incident of 10 Jan 1940); the revised plan (Manstein's proposal, taken up after his meeting with Hitler of 17 Feb; OKH deployment directive of 24 Feb 1940) is the decision of this quarter. Nature: none, no campaign this quarter. WEST: arms_WEST high visible from this tick. The Allied plans for Scandinavia (Supreme War Council, 5 Feb 1940) and the German-Soviet economic agreement of 11 Feb 1940 are not separate rows.
source: OKH deployment directive Case Yellow, 24 Feb 1940 (in Jacobsen, Dokumente zur Vorgeschichte des Westfeldzuges, 1956); Halder war diary

note: GER: offensive launched 10 May 1940. Nature: campaign_west, breakthrough at Sedan 13 to 15 May, Dunkirk 26 May to 4 Jun, armistice 22 Jun 1940 (in force 25 Jun). WEST: War Cabinet meetings of 26 to 28 May 1940 on an approach to Mussolini; decision of 28 May to fight on. USSR: rearm, the conference on the lessons of the Finnish war (Apr 1940) and Timoshenko's appointment as Commissar of Defence (7 May 1940); effect after the horizon. The Soviet occupation of the Baltic states (15 to 17 Jun) and of Bessarabia and Northern Bukovina (28 Jun) is not modeled. Norway (from 9 Apr) and Italy's entry (10 Jun) are not modeled.
source: CAB 65 War Cabinet conclusions and confidential annexes, 26 to 28 May 1940; Lukacs 1999; Franco-German armistice of 22 Jun 1940

note: GER: Directive No. 16 (16 Jul, Sea Lion) and No. 17 (1 Aug 1940); main air offensive from 13 Aug. The Reichstag offer of 19 Jul 1940 (offer_terms_britain) and the Second Vienna Award of 30 Aug are second GER actions. WEST: Halifax's broadcast rejection of the offer, 22 Jul 1940. Nature: destroyers-for-bases agreement 2 Sep 1940. JPN: the Tripartite Pact (27 Sep 1940) and the move into northern Indochina are not modeled.
source: Trevor-Roper (ed.), Hitler's War Directives, Directives No. 16 and 17; Reichstag speech of 19 Jul 1940; FRUS 1940 vol. III (destroyers for bases)

note: GER: German military mission to Romania (Oct 1940); Hungary (20 Nov), Romania (23 Nov) and Slovakia (24 Nov) adhere to the Tripartite Pact. Nature: Sea Lion postponed indefinitely 17 Sep and to spring 1941 on 12 Oct 1940; the daylight battle is usually dated to 31 Oct; part of the resolution falls in 1940Q3 [SQR in part]. USSR: Molotov in Berlin 12 to 13 Nov 1940 and the Soviet conditions of 25 Nov; no accession (join_axis needs aims_USSR == opportunist, excluded by the default assumption). WEST: idle, the decision to fight on stands. Italy's attack on Greece (28 Oct 1940) is not modeled.
source: DGFP Series D vol. XI; Nazi-Soviet Relations 1939-1941; Trevor-Roper (ed.), Hitler's War Directives
